# RFC-0002: Agent-Ergonomic MCP Service Contract

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Tyler Michael Smith

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0002:C-PURPOSE] Purpose and caller model (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-purpose"></a>

This RFC defines the public contract for MCP services in nm-hard-tools. The primary caller is an autonomous agent that must discover operator-approved capabilities, make safe choices with limited context, resume asynchronous work, and interpret results without repository knowledge. The contract favors a small predictable tool vocabulary, structured data, explicit side effects, and useful recovery information.

### [RFC-0002:C-SCOPE] Scope and non-goals (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-scope"></a>

This RFC governs MCP discovery, tool naming, input and output schemas, operation lifecycle, artifact access, errors, safety metadata, and compatibility across the evaluation and benchmark services. It does not prescribe private Python types, Kubernetes object layouts, REST routes, storage engines, deployment topology, or agent prompting strategy. MCP is an agent-facing product surface rather than a mechanical projection of an internal API.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0002:C-SERVICE-BOUNDARIES] Bounded domain services (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-service-boundaries"></a>

Each MCP server MUST represent one coherent operator-owned domain and MUST identify that domain in its advertised server name and instructions. A server MUST expose only capabilities that share an authorization and operational boundary. The evaluation and forward-benchmark domains MAY remain separate servers, but both MUST implement the common lifecycle and representation rules in this RFC. A server MUST NOT expose an internal REST operation solely because that operation exists.

### [RFC-0002:C-PROTOCOL-DISCOVERY] Protocol and server discovery (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-protocol-discovery"></a>

Each server MUST support MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`. Its `server/discover` result MUST expose `supportedVersions`, `capabilities`, `instructions`, `ttlMs`, and `cacheScope` as defined by that protocol version. Every result MUST expose the stable server name and service version in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"].name` and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"].version`. Advertised capabilities MUST match the methods and content types the server actually supports. Requests MUST be independent of conversational or transport session state; any state needed by a later call MUST be represented by an explicit opaque reference returned to the caller. Server instructions MUST state the preferred workflow, the authorization boundary, and the result-size strategy in no more than 1,024 Unicode characters.

### [RFC-0002:C-TOOL-FAMILIES] Common tool families (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-tool-families"></a>

The evaluation server MUST expose `get_evaluation_capabilities`, `plan_evaluation`, `submit_evaluation`, `list_evaluations`, `get_evaluation`, `cancel_evaluation`, `list_evaluation_artifacts`, `get_evaluation_report`, `inspect_evaluation_result`, `query_evaluation_artifact`, and `compare_evaluations`. The forward-benchmark server MUST expose `get_benchmark_capabilities`, `plan_benchmark`, `submit_benchmark`, `list_benchmarks`, `get_benchmark`, `cancel_benchmark`, `list_benchmark_artifacts`, `get_benchmark_report`, `inspect_benchmark_result`, `query_benchmark_artifact`, and `compare_benchmarks`. Additional tools MUST represent a complete caller goal, use a verb-first snake_case name, and MUST NOT require knowledge of an internal route, controller, Job, filename, or storage layout.

### [RFC-0002:C-CAPABILITY-CATALOG] Discoverable operator capabilities (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-capability-catalog"></a>

`get_<domain>_capabilities` MUST be read-only and MUST return the operator-approved choices, defaults, bounds, mutually dependent constraints, enabled optional features, operation and artifact retention periods, result-view descriptors defined by [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-DISCOVERY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-inspection-discovery), artifact query modes defined by [RFC-0002:C-ARTIFACT-QUERY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-artifact-query), and a minimal valid request template needed to construct a plan. Choices MUST include stable machine identifiers and short caller-facing descriptions. When a catalog cannot fit in one bounded result, the tool MUST support filtering or cursor pagination and MUST report truncation explicitly. A caller MUST NOT need deployment files, documentation, trial-and-error validation, artifact filenames, or a separate non-MCP API to discover a valid request or inspection.

### [RFC-0002:C-TOOL-METADATA] Tool selection metadata (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-tool-metadata"></a>

Every tool MUST provide a stable name, a title, a description, an input schema, an output schema, and MCP tool annotations. Each output schema MUST use JSON Schema composition to accept exactly one of the tool's successful `structuredContent` shape or the common tool-error shape defined by [RFC-0002:C-ERRORS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-errors). A description MUST say when to use the tool, its material side effect or lack thereof, its principal prerequisite, and what the successful result enables. `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, and `openWorldHint` MUST accurately describe observable behavior. Tools MUST be returned in deterministic name order.

### [RFC-0002:C-INPUT-SCHEMAS] Agent-constructible inputs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-input-schemas"></a>

Tool inputs MUST use structured JSON fields for semantic values and MUST NOT require YAML, shell fragments, command-line arguments, or an encoded internal request as the primary interface. Every fixed-shape input object MUST reject unknown properties. Fields MUST use semantic names, explicit formats, enums where the choice set is closed, and unit-bearing names such as `timeout_seconds` where a number has a unit. Optional fields MUST declare their default behavior. Secrets MUST NOT be accepted as tool arguments. An input schema MUST include descriptions for fields whose meaning is not evident from the field name.

### [RFC-0002:C-PLAN] Exact preview before mutation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-plan"></a>

`plan_<domain>` MUST validate and resolve a complete request without creating, queuing, cancelling, or otherwise mutating domain work. A successful plan MUST return an opaque `plan_ref`, a stable `plan_digest`, the canonical resolved request, requested resources, placement or queue implications when applicable, estimated scope, warnings, and `expires_at` when the plan can expire. The canonical resolved request MUST make every applied default visible. The plan result MUST contain enough information for an agent and user to understand the material work that submission would authorize.

### [RFC-0002:C-SUBMIT] Plan-bound idempotent submission (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-submit"></a>

`submit_<domain>` MUST accept the `plan_ref` produced by `plan_<domain>` and MUST NOT require the caller to repeat the planned request. Submission MUST execute exactly the canonical request identified by `plan_digest`. The first successful submission of a `plan_ref` MUST atomically bind that reference to exactly one operation. Every later authorized submission of that reference, including concurrent submission and submission after plan expiry, MUST return the bound operation rather than create duplicate work. Expiry, staleness, authorization, and feasibility checks apply before the binding is created; a failed pre-binding check MUST create no work and MUST return the applicable error from [RFC-0002:C-ERRORS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-errors). Successful submission MUST return the common operation status defined by [RFC-0002:C-OPERATION-STATUS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-operation-status).

### [RFC-0002:C-OPERATION-STATUS] Self-contained asynchronous status (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-operation-status"></a>

Every submit, get, and cancel result MUST include a stable domain operation identifier, `state`, `terminal`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, a concise `summary`, and `available_actions`. The common `state` values MUST be `queued`, `running`, `cancelling`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled`; domain-specific detail MUST use a separate `state_detail` field. `terminal` MUST be true exactly when `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. `queued` MAY transition to any other state, `running` MAY transition to `cancelling`, `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`, and `cancelling` MAY transition to `cancelled` or `failed`; terminal states MUST NOT transition. A nonterminal result MUST include `poll_after_ms` or an explicit event subscription reference. A terminal result MUST identify report and artifact availability. Each `available_actions` entry MUST contain `tool_name` and complete safe `arguments` using only values already known to the server; an empty array MUST be returned when no action is available.

### [RFC-0002:C-LIST] Bounded resumable listing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-list"></a>

`list_<domain-plural>` MUST return bounded operation summaries using deterministic ordering and cursor-based pagination. A first-page request MUST establish a fixed traversal snapshot, and every cursor derived from it MUST traverse each member of that snapshot exactly once in the documented order even when operations are created or updated concurrently. It MUST support filters for identifier, state, creation time, and operator-defined labels when those labels exist. A page MUST state whether more results exist and MUST provide `next_cursor` when they do. A cursor MUST be opaque to callers. An invalid or expired cursor MUST return `INVALID_CURSOR` with a suggested action that restarts the listing. Each summary MUST contain the operation identifier, state, terminal flag, creation and update times, and a concise request identity sufficient to choose an item for `get_<domain>`.

### [RFC-0002:C-CANCELLATION] Safe cancellation semantics (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-cancellation"></a>

`cancel_<domain>` MUST be idempotent and MUST preserve the operation record and completed artifacts. Cancelling a terminal operation MUST return its current status without changing it. Cancelling an active operation MUST return the resulting or transitional status and MUST NOT claim completion before cancellation is durable. The tool MUST be annotated as destructive because it stops intended work, even though the operation record is retained.

### [RFC-0002:C-RESULT-REPRESENTATION] Token-efficient structured results (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-result-representation"></a>

Every tool call that includes `structuredContent` MUST conform to the tool's advertised output schema. A successful result MUST match the schema's success branch, and a result with `isError: true` MUST match only the common tool-error branch in [RFC-0002:C-ERRORS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-errors). Text content MUST be a concise caller-facing summary and MUST NOT duplicate a serialization of the complete structured result for protocol version `2026-07-28`. Text content SHOULD be no more than 1,024 Unicode characters. Every versioned domain success result MUST include `schema_version`. Timestamps MUST use RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, byte counts MUST be integers, and durations and rates MUST identify their units in field names.

### [RFC-0002:C-BOUNDED-RESULTS] Progressive disclosure and result bounds (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-bounded-results"></a>

Every tool result MUST be bounded by a documented service limit. When a logical result exceeds that limit, the server MUST return a useful summary plus pagination, a narrower follow-up query, or artifact references; it MUST NOT return only an oversize error when a bounded representation is available. List results MUST omit bulky bodies. Reports and semantic inspection views MUST prioritize decision-relevant metrics, provenance, warnings, and links over raw samples, logs, traces, or manifests. Pagination state MUST use `has_more` and `next_cursor` and MUST be independent of evidence fidelity. `completeness: complete` means the full query snapshot contains all matching evidence, even when the current page is not final. `truncated` means matching evidence was permanently omitted from the snapshot, `sampled` means the snapshot contains a disclosed selection of matching evidence, and `approximate` means at least one returned value is an estimate. Any non-complete result MUST include `completeness_reason` and `omitted_scope`; sampled or approximate results MUST also identify their method.

### [RFC-0002:C-ARTIFACTS] Artifact-oriented detail access (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-artifacts"></a>

`list_<domain>_artifacts` MUST return immutable artifact metadata including `artifact_ref`, semantic `artifact_kind`, name, media type, byte size, digest, schema identifier and version when structured, creation time, retention expiry when applicable, query-mode descriptors, and `available_actions`. Each query-mode descriptor MUST contain a discriminant, self-contained parameter and result JSON Schemas, defaults, maximum page size, deterministic ordering, maximum bytes or records scanned, maximum time span when applicable, and execution deadline. Each available action MUST contain a tool name and complete safe arguments for an inspection that can be performed on that artifact. `get_<domain>_report` MUST return the bounded structured terminal report rather than a filesystem path or raw archive. Bulky artifacts SHOULD be exposed as MCP resource links when the negotiated protocol supports them. If direct resource reading is unsupported, the metadata MUST identify the supported retrieval mechanism without exposing credentials. An operation or artifact removed under the advertised retention policy MUST return `REFERENCE_EXPIRED`; a reference that never existed or is not visible to the caller MUST return `NOT_FOUND` without revealing which condition applies.

### [RFC-0002:C-ERRORS] Actionable stable errors (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-errors"></a>

Invalid MCP envelopes, authentication failures, unknown tools, unsupported methods, and protocol negotiation failures MUST use protocol-level errors. A recognized tool that cannot complete its domain action MUST return `isError: true` and `structuredContent` matching the tool output schema's common error branch. That branch MUST be a closed object with required string `code`, required string `message`, required boolean `retryable`, nullable integer `retry_after_ms`, required array `field_issues`, nullable string `current_state`, and nullable object `suggested_action`. Each field issue MUST be a closed object containing string `field`, string `code`, and string `message`. A suggested action MUST be a closed object containing `tool_name` and complete safe `arguments`, or be null. RFC-owned codes MUST include `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `PLAN_EXPIRED`, `PLAN_STALE`, `PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE`, `INVALID_CURSOR`, `NOT_FOUND`, `REFERENCE_EXPIRED`, `STATE_CONFLICT`, `RESULT_NOT_READY`, `INCOMPATIBLE_RESULTS`, `QUERY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, and `INTERNAL_ERROR`. Domain-specific codes MUST be prefixed `EVALUATION_` or `BENCHMARK_`. Multi-operation errors MUST place readiness and incompatibility diagnostics in `field_issues` using stable paths such as `operation_ids[2]`; `current_state` MUST be null for multi-operation errors. `PLAN_EXPIRED`, `PLAN_STALE`, and `PLAN_NOT_FEASIBLE` MUST suggest the applicable plan tool; `INVALID_CURSOR` MUST suggest restarting the applicable listing, inspection, artifact-query, or comparison tool. `retry_after_ms` MUST be non-null for a retryable rate limit and SHOULD be non-null for a transient dependency failure. Error content MUST NOT expose credentials, stack traces, internal network locations, or unbounded upstream bodies.

### [RFC-0002:C-AUTHORIZATION] Authorization and open-world safety (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-authorization"></a>

Servers MUST authenticate requests before parsing or executing tool arguments when authentication is configured. Tool results and catalogs MUST reveal only choices and artifacts authorized for the caller. The server MUST select credentials, endpoints, datasets, queues, images, and cluster policy from operator-controlled configuration or catalog identifiers rather than caller-provided secrets or arbitrary locations. A tool MUST set `openWorldHint` to false unless it can contact destinations outside the operator-defined environment as a direct consequence of caller input.

### [RFC-0002:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility and evolution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-compatibility"></a>

Published tool names, required input fields, field meanings, state meanings, error codes, and structured output fields MUST remain backward compatible within a service major version. Additive optional object fields MAY be introduced within a major version. Adding, removing, or changing an output enum value is a breaking change unless the field was specified as an open string vocabulary with mandatory unknown-value handling. A breaking change MUST use a new service major version or a new tool name and MUST leave the prior surface discoverable for a documented migration window. `schema_version` MUST change when a persisted report or artifact schema changes, and readers MUST be able to distinguish supported from unsupported versions.

### [RFC-0002:C-CONFORMANCE] Agent-journey conformance (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-conformance"></a>

Each service MUST maintain automated conformance coverage for these caller journeys: discover a minimal valid request without external documentation; plan without mutation; concurrently submit the exact plan and bind it to one operation; resubmit the bound plan after expiry without duplicate work; resume a nonterminal operation using only returned identifiers; cancel twice safely; page a fixed listing snapshot without gaps or duplicates while operations change; restart after an invalid cursor; discover and inspect every common semantic result view without knowing artifact filenames; follow an artifact action into a bounded query; page a structured query without gaps or duplicates; compare compatible results with explicit units and baseline; reject incompatible comparison; obtain a raw artifact reference when semantic views are insufficient; correct an invalid field from the returned error; recover from an expired unbound plan; observe retention expiry; and distinguish retryable from non-retryable failure. Conformance MUST validate advertised success schemas, common tool-error fields, annotations, available-action arguments, inspection provenance, completeness markers, and query bounds against observed results and side effects.

---

## 3. Result Inspection

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-MODEL] Layered result inspection (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-model"></a>

Agents normally ask semantic questions such as which metric regressed, why an operation failed, or which configuration produced a result. Artifact filenames and serialization formats are storage concerns, not the primary agent interface. Services therefore expose semantic result views first, bounded structured artifact queries second, and raw resource access as an escape hatch. This preserves a consistent workflow while allowing domain-specific evidence.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-DISCOVERY] Discoverable inspection views (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-discovery"></a>

Each capability catalog MUST advertise every supported result view. A view descriptor MUST contain stable `view_id`, `title`, `description`, applicable operation states, required artifact kinds, self-contained JSON Schema 2020-12 `parameters_schema` and `data_schema`, `supports_comparison`, default and maximum page sizes, deterministic default ordering, and a stability value of `live` or `immutable`. A comparison-enabled descriptor MUST additionally define stable alignment keys; comparable measures with field, unit, `ratio_comparable`, and improvement direction of `higher`, `lower`, or `neutral`; fields that MUST be equal for compatibility; and report-only context fields. Alignment keys MUST identify at most one comparable row per operation unless the descriptor defines a deterministic aggregation, its input field, aggregation function, null handling, and output unit. The common view identifiers MUST be `overview`, `configuration`, `provenance`, `metrics`, and `failures`. Both services MUST support every common view. A state-applicable view with no matching data MUST return a complete empty result rather than be omitted. Evaluation-specific views MAY include `samples` and `task_metrics`. Benchmark-specific views MAY include `performance`, `kernels`, `traces`, and `timeline`. View identifiers, schemas, semantic keys, units, and meanings MUST remain compatible under [RFC-0002:C-COMPATIBILITY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-compatibility).

### [RFC-0002:C-SEMANTIC-INSPECTION] Semantic result inspection (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-semantic-inspection"></a>

`inspect_evaluation_result` and `inspect_benchmark_result` MUST accept either a first-call object containing the domain operation identifier, a discovered `view_id`, view `parameters`, and optional `page_size`, or a continuation object containing only `cursor`. The server MUST validate parameters against the advertised view schema and MUST return `INVALID_ARGUMENT` field issues for violations. Inspecting before an operation can reach an applicable state MUST return `RESULT_NOT_READY`. Inspecting an operation whose terminal state cannot support the view MUST return `STATE_CONFLICT`. A successful result MUST contain `operation_id`, `view_id`, `view_schema_id`, `view_schema_version`, `as_of`, `summary`, `data`, `completeness`, `completeness_reason`, `omitted_scope`, `has_more`, `next_cursor`, and `source_artifacts`; `data` MUST conform to the advertised `data_schema`. `has_more` MUST be true exactly when `next_cursor` is non-null. Every source artifact entry MUST contain `artifact_ref` and digest. Inspection MUST be read-only. While its cursor, operation, and artifacts remain valid under advertised retention policies, repeating an immutable-view request MUST return semantically identical data.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-PAGINATION] Stable inspection pagination (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-pagination"></a>

A semantic inspection, artifact query, or comparison that returns ordered items MUST use opaque cursor pagination. The first call MUST establish a fixed query snapshot, resolved schemas, ordering, and page size. Derived cursors MUST preserve those choices and MUST traverse each matching item exactly once. The service MUST apply a deterministic default order and MUST report that order in the result. A continuation call MUST accept the cursor as its only required argument and MUST NOT require the caller to repeat the original query. Supplying query arguments with a continuation cursor MUST return `INVALID_CURSOR`. An expired cursor MUST return `INVALID_CURSOR` with a suggested action containing the original safe first-call arguments without the cursor.

### [RFC-0002:C-ARTIFACT-QUERY] Bounded structured artifact queries (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-artifact-query"></a>

`query_evaluation_artifact` and `query_benchmark_artifact` MUST accept either a first-call object containing `artifact_ref`, exactly one advertised query variant, and optional `page_size`, or a continuation object containing only `cursor`. `page_size` MUST default to the query-mode descriptor's default and MUST be between one and its advertised maximum. `json_pointer` MUST use RFC 6901 syntax and select one bounded subtree. Text lines MUST be decoded as UTF-8 with replacement, numbered from one, and ordered by increasing line number. `text_search` MUST use a non-empty literal, default `case_sensitive` to false, and bound preceding and following context lines. `line_range` MUST use inclusive `start_line` and positive `line_count`. `table` MUST use advertised columns and typed `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, and `gte` filters combined by logical AND. `time_range` MUST use RFC 3339 `start_inclusive` and `end_exclusive` values and order equal timestamps by stable source position. Query inputs MUST NOT accept executable code, regular expressions, SQL, jq, JSONPath, shell syntax, or implementation-specific expressions. Before expensive work, the service MUST reject a query that exceeds a statically checkable advertised scan, time-span, column, context, or page-size bound with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; its field issue MUST identify the bound and its suggested action MUST contain a safe narrower query. The service MUST enforce the advertised execution deadline at runtime. Reaching that deadline before producing a valid page MUST return non-retryable `QUERY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` with a safe narrower suggested query and MUST NOT return an unmarked partial page. Results MUST contain artifact identity and digest, normalized query, result schema identifier and version, ordering, `data`, `completeness`, `completeness_reason`, `omitted_scope`, `has_more`, and `next_cursor`; `data` MUST conform to the advertised query result schema. A query MUST NOT mutate an artifact or silently scan a different artifact version.

### [RFC-0002:C-RESULT-COMPARISON] Cross-operation comparison (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-result-comparison"></a>

`compare_evaluations` and `compare_benchmarks` MUST accept either a first-call object containing between two and eight domain operation identifiers, a required `baseline_operation_id` drawn from those identifiers, a discovered comparison-enabled view, view parameters, and optional `page_size`, or a continuation object containing only `cursor`. The server MUST validate view parameters against the advertised `parameters_schema` and MUST return `INVALID_ARGUMENT` field issues for violations. An operation that may still reach a comparison-applicable state MUST produce `RESULT_NOT_READY` with a field issue for its indexed identifier; a terminal operation that cannot support the view MUST produce `STATE_CONFLICT`. Comparison MUST align values by the descriptor's stable alignment keys. Duplicate alignment keys without the descriptor-defined aggregation MUST return `INCOMPATIBLE_RESULTS` with indexed field issues. Every required-equal compatibility field MUST match or the service MUST return `INCOMPATIBLE_RESULTS` with field issues for each mismatch. Differences in report-only context fields MAY be compared but MUST be returned structurally. For each finite numeric candidate and baseline with the same unit, `absolute_delta` MUST equal candidate minus baseline. `relative_delta` MUST equal `absolute_delta / abs(baseline)` when the baseline is nonzero and the measure declares `ratio_comparable: true`; otherwise it MUST be null with `relative_delta_reason`. Improvement or regression MUST be derived from the measure's advertised improvement direction and MUST be `neutral` when that direction is neutral. Missing, nonnumeric, nonfinite, sampled, and approximate values MUST remain explicit and MUST NOT be silently coerced. The bounded paginated result MUST identify the operations, baseline, view schema, ordering, units, aligned values, missing values, context differences, deltas, `completeness`, `completeness_reason`, `omitted_scope`, `has_more`, and `next_cursor`; sampled or approximate values MUST identify their method.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-PROVENANCE] Inspection evidence and explainability (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-provenance"></a>

Every semantic inspection and comparison result MUST identify the operation configuration digest, source artifact references and digests, result or view schema version, query parameters after defaults, and snapshot time. Derived, sampled, or approximate values MUST identify the derivation method and source fields. A service-generated summary MUST be deterministic from the returned evidence and MUST distinguish observed values from derived values. The service MUST NOT present an unsupported causal explanation as artifact evidence.
